description: Vertical edge focusing of a beta=20deg parallelogram dipole extracted from a 3D reduced-Omega FEM mid-plane map by closed-orbit (symmetric) tracking with window decomposition, compared against the x-uniform tilted-fringe model built from the FEM's own mid-line profile and against the SCOFF/Enge closed form tan(beta_eff - psi)/rho.  Generated by the PART B machinery of docs/clebsch_hodograph/edge_focusing_tracking.py (fem_scoff_study).

config.magnet: parallelogram poles (both edges tilted by beta), gap 0.040 m, pole half-width 0.12 m, L 0.20 m, centered return legs (y in +/-0.05), mu_r 1000 linear
config.coil: explicit rounded-parallelogram pair following the pole outline at 0.02 m normal offset (sides x=+/-0.08, corner arcs r=0.02, NI=10 kA per loop); CoilBuilder.mirror() NOT used (broken straights), rad.TrfOrnt NOT used (RadiaField heap corruption)
config.solver: reduced-Omega H1 order 2, sparsecholesky, maxh air 0.035 / iron 0.014 / beam box 0.008 / pole gap-edge lines 0.004; mid-plane sampled 81x401 over +/-0.05 x +/-0.26 m; C2 map symmetrization
config.tracker: RK4 ds=5e-4 m, symmetric (closed-orbit) traversal, Hill-integral window decomposition (T1 transverse-gradient + T2 edge-crossing)

headline.error_budget: the -5..-7 pct deficit vs the x-uniform model is ENGINE-INDEPENDENT (dK_in/model = 0.933 reduced-Omega, 0.919/0.948 HDiv-VIM at edge mesh 4/2.5 mm; absolute dK_in scatter across engines/meshes ~+-3 pct) and is REAL 3D physics, not mesh error: the local iso-field tilt of the entrance fringe near x=0 is only ~0.95-0.96 of the geometric tan(beta) -- measured directly on both engines' maps (corner arcs + coil side bars + finite pole width) -- so the x-uniform tilted-fringe model and hard-edge/SCOFF bookkeeping with the geometric beta overpredict the edge focusing by ~5 pct; dK_in*rho constant to ~1 pct over rho 5..40 (fixed mesh), beta=0 spurious floor +0.0013 reduced-Omega / +0.0002 HDiv-fine (2026-07-13 HDiv-VIM cross-check; the earlier iron-mesh-error attribution is RETRACTED)

hdiv_vim_cross_check.engine: FEEC HDiv-VIM (radia.vim.MeshSoftIron, rad.Solve auto dispatch, RT1): iron-only tet mesh, no air discretization, exact open boundary; mid-plane map by one batch rad.Fld (analytic surface-charge integrals of the solved per-element M + coil Biot-Savart); same explicit CoilBuilder pair and identical downstream measurement chain (hdiv_scoff_study in edge_focusing_tracking.py)

engine_agreement.note: two independent field engines (different formulation, mesh, boundary treatment) reproduce the entrance-window dK_in to 0.8% at matched edge-mesh density (2.7% at the finer HDiv edge mesh -- the cross-engine/mesh scatter of the absolute dK is ~+-3%); the deficit vs the x-uniform model persists in ALL configurations (ratio 0.92-0.95), so it is physics, not solver discretization error

iso_field_tilt_probe_beta20.definition: entrance-fringe iso-field line slope dy/dx fitted over |x|<=10.5 mm at g=0.2/0.5/0.8, divided by -tan(beta); the x-uniform model assumes exactly 1.0
iso_field_tilt_probe_beta20.note: the real magnet's local iso-field tilt near the beam is only ~0.95-0.96 of the geometric edge angle (reduced-Omega 0.95-0.96 level-independent; HDiv converges to the same value with edge refinement, g=0.5: 0.89 -> 0.95) -- corner arcs + coil side bars + finite pole width; this reduced effective edge angle is the deficit mechanism, and it is a real magnet-design quantity: hard-edge/SCOFF bookkeeping with the GEOMETRIC beta overpredicts the vertical edge focusing by ~5 pct for this geometry

hdiv_vim_cross_check.fringe_shape_caveat: RESOLVED 2026-07-14 (see mesh_dependence_diagnosis): the slow fringe-shape convergence was the piecewise-constant-M ripple of bulk-size gap-face elements at 20 mm standoff; gap-face refinement face_maxh=0.006 cures it (g_max 1.0001, K1g 8.80 vs reduced-Omega 8.85 mm).  B0 remains relative-only (+-3.5% near-field-evaluation scatter, global demag constant to 5 digits).

mesh_dependence_diagnosis.method: separation runs at beta=0 varying maxh_iron / edge_maxh / gap-face face_maxh independently (identical chain); reference reduced-Omega scoff9: B0=0.4412 T, K1g=8.85 mm, g_max=1.0004
findings: K1g is EDGE-resolution dominated and converges within HDiv at edge_maxh<=2.5 mm (7.84/7.85/7.78 mm for maxh 14/11 and edge 2.5/1.5) -- but sticks ~12% below the reduced-Omega value until the gap FACE is refined.

The flat-top-edge overshoot (g_max 1.02-1.04) does NOT respond to edge refinement (1.026 at edge 1.5 mm): it sits 30 mm inside the pole end, above BULK-size gap-face elements.  It is the piecewise-constant-M ripple of those elements at 20 mm standoff (rad.Fld write-back collapses the RT1 solution to per-element constant M).

CURE: refining the gap-facing pole faces to face_maxh=0.006 (~standoff/3) removes the ripple: g_max 1.0245 -> 1.0001 and K1g 7.84 -> 8.80 mm, matching the reduced-Omega 8.85 mm to 0.6% (run hx_f).  The 12% cross-engine K1g gap was entirely this ripple.

LIMIT: face_maxh=0.004 at bulk 14 mm (size contrast ~3.5x) drives the mass-Riesz CG past its 4000-iteration cap (fail-loud RuntimeError, n_face=598650).  Keep the face/bulk contrast <= ~2.5x, or lower maxh_iron together with face_maxh.

RESIDUAL: B0 scatters +-3.5% across ALL configurations (0.425..0.456 T; non-monotone) while the global demag probe is constant to 5 digits (0.45022..0.45025) -- the global M is mesh-independent and the scatter is a NEAR-FIELD-EVALUATION sensitivity of the gap field.  It first-order-cancels in the B0-normalized dK measurement (kappa=1/(B0 rho) rescales tracked and model kicks alike); do not quote the HDiv B0 absolute value.
CG conditioning degrades on graded meshes: iters 45-49 (uniform maxh 14), 211-222 (maxh 11), 614 (face 6 mm at bulk 14 mm).
mesh_dependence_diagnosis.prescription: for near-surface map evaluation (standoff ~ GAP/2), set face_maxh ~ standoff/3 on the source faces facing the map, keep face/bulk size contrast <= ~2.5x, and treat B0 as relative-only; dK and the iso-field tilt are robust without any of this (+-3%)
mesh_dependence_diagnosis.root_cause_note: the ripple is ultimately the per-element constant-M collapse in the rad.Fld write-back (ObjSetM) of the RT1 solution; evaluating the field from the RT1 (linear-M) solution directly -- radia.vim already ships arbitrary-degree charge kernels (tet_volume_field_polynomial / polynomial_triangle_charge_field) -- would remove the O(h) collapse error without mesh prescriptions; flagged as a radia improvement task
